statement: Comparison and pre-emption verdict for U023: the closest legal benchmark cannot be re-labelled to version-level retrieval evaluation, because its items are multiple-choice questions with answer-option gold labels built from pairs of EUR-Lex passages and their relations, and its grounding axis supplies authoritative reference context rather than requiring a retriever to select among candidate versions. Extending it to version-level retrieval would require new construction - version chains and per-clause in-force intervals with version-identity labels on a candidate pool - not re-labelling. More strongly, the same paper states that retrieval-oriented legal benchmarks do not assess whether retrieved provisions remain in force, which confirms the gap rather than filling it. The pre-emption concern is therefore not realized, but the benchmark must be built from an EUR-Lex-like source with clause-level validity metadata; the difference from the closest work is a genuine difference in evaluation object (which version was retrieved) rather than an implementation detail.
